claim: PMA (phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate) is a tumor promoter that activates macropinocytosis.
source: Here, we show that a macropinocytosis activator, the tumor promoter phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), enhances Wnt signaling.
evidence: The manuscript states that PMA is a macropinocytosis activator and tumor promoter, supported by citation to Swanson, 1989.

claim: PMA enhances canonical Wnt signaling.
source: Here, we show that a macropinocytosis activator, the tumor promoter phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), enhances Wnt signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through multiple experiments in the manuscript.

claim: PMA cooperates with Wnt signaling in Xenopus embryos.
source: Experiments using the Xenopus embryo as an in vivo model showed marked cooperation between the PMA phorbol ester and Wnt signaling, which was blocked by inhibitors of macropinocytosis, Rac1 activity, and lysosome acidification.
evidence: Demonstrated through embryo experiments showing synergistic dorsalization effects.

claim: The cooperation between PMA and Wnt signaling is blocked by macropinocytosis inhibitors.
source: Experiments using the Xenopus embryo as an in vivo model showed marked cooperation between the PMA phorbol ester and Wnt signaling, which was blocked by inhibitors of macropinocytosis, Rac1 activity, and lysosome acidification.
evidence: EIPA treatment blocked the synergistic effects of PMA and LiCl in embryos.

claim: The cooperation between PMA and Wnt signaling is blocked by Rac1 inhibitors.
source: Experiments using the Xenopus embryo as an in vivo model showed marked cooperation between the PMA phorbol ester and Wnt signaling, which was blocked by inhibitors of macropinocytosis, Rac1 activity, and lysosome acidification.
evidence: EHT1864 (Rac1 inhibitor) blocked Wnt signaling effects in embryos.

claim: The cooperation between PMA and Wnt signaling is blocked by lysosome acidification inhibitors.
source: Experiments using the Xenopus embryo as an in vivo model showed marked cooperation between the PMA phorbol ester and Wnt signaling, which was blocked by inhibitors of macropinocytosis, Rac1 activity, and lysosome acidification.
evidence: Bafilomycin A treatment blocked the synergistic effects of PMA and LiCl.

claim: Human colorectal cancer progression correlates with increased macropinocytosis/multivesicular body/lysosome markers.
source: Human colorectal cancer tissue arrays and xenografts in mice showed a correlation of cancer progression with increased macropinocytosis/multivesicular body/lysosome markers and decreased GSK3 levels.
evidence: Tissue array immunostaining showed increased Pak1, CD63, and V0a3 with cancer grade.

claim: Human colorectal cancer progression correlates with decreased GSK3 levels.
source: Human colorectal cancer tissue arrays and xenografts in mice showed a correlation of cancer progression with increased macropinocytosis/multivesicular body/lysosome markers and decreased GSK3 levels.
evidence: Tissue array immunostaining showed decreased GSK3 with increasing cancer malignancy.

claim: PMA was first purified from croton oil as the active tumor-promoting agent.
source: The active agent in croton oil was later purified and found to be the phorbol ester phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), also known as 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13-acetate (TPA).
evidence: Historical context provided with implicit citation to earlier work.

claim: PMA activates protein kinase C (PKC) in the plasma membrane by mimicking diacylglycerol (DAG).
source: The molecular mechanism by which PMA promotes cancer is incompletely understood but involves the activation of protein kinase C (PKC) in the plasma membrane, where PMA mimics the endogenous second messenger diacylglycerol (DAG) (Nishizuka, 1984).
evidence: Cited from Nishizuka, 1984.

claim: Tumor promoters cause chronic inflammation and contribute to tumorigenesis.
source: Tumor promoters cause chronic inflammation and significantly contribute to tumorigenesis (Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007).
evidence: Cited from Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007.

claim: The canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway is a major driver of cancer.
source: The canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway is a major driver of cancer and plays a crucial role in embryonic development (MacDonald et al., 2009; Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: Cited from MacDonald et al., 2009 and Nusse and Clevers, 2017.

claim: The canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway plays a crucial role in embryonic development.
source: The canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway is a major driver of cancer and plays a crucial role in embryonic development (MacDonald et al., 2009; Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: Cited from MacDonald et al., 2009 and Nusse and Clevers, 2017.

claim: Most colon cancers are initiated by mutation of the tumor suppressor Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC).
source: In the case of colon cancer, the great majority of tumors are initiated by mutation of the tumor suppressor Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC), which is a component of the destruction complex that normally degrades the transcriptional regulator β-catenin, leading to its accumulation in the nucleus and benign polyp formation (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996; Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006).
evidence: Cited from Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996 and Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006.

claim: APC is a component of the destruction complex that normally degrades β-catenin.
source: In the case of colon cancer, the great majority of tumors are initiated by mutation of the tumor suppressor Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC), which is a component of the destruction complex that normally degrades the transcriptional regulator β-catenin, leading to its accumulation in the nucleus and benign polyp formation (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996; Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006).
evidence: Cited from Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996 and Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006.

claim: APC mutation leads to β-catenin accumulation in the nucleus and benign polyp formation.
source: In the case of colon cancer, the great majority of tumors are initiated by mutation of the tumor suppressor Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC), which is a component of the destruction complex that normally degrades the transcriptional regulator β-catenin, leading to its accumulation in the nucleus and benign polyp formation (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996; Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006).
evidence: Cited from Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996 and Segditsas and Tomlinson, 2006.

claim: GSK3 phosphorylates β-catenin, leading to its degradation in the proteasome.
source: A key regulator of Wnt signaling is Glycogen Synthetase 3 (GSK3), which phosphorylates β-catenin, leading to the formation of a phosphodegron that triggers its degradation in the proteasome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Wnt pathway mechanism.

claim: Upon Wnt receptor activation, GSK3 is sequestered into multivesicular bodies (MVBs).
source: Upon activation of the Wnt receptors, GSK3, together with the destruction complex, is sequestered into multivesicular bodies (MVBs), also known as the late endosomes (Taelman et al., 2010; Vinyoles et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from Taelman et al., 2010 and Vinyoles et al., 2014.

claim: GSK3 sequestration into MVBs/lysosomes leads to stabilization of many cellular proteins in addition to β-catenin.
source: The translocation of GSK3 from the cytosol into MVBs/lysosomes leads to the stabilization of many other cellular proteins in addition to β-catenin, in a process designated Wnt-STOP (Wnt-Stabilization of Proteins) (Acebron et al., 2014; Albrecht et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from Acebron et al., 2014 and Albrecht et al., 2021.

claim: GSK3 phosphorylation targets stabilized by Wnt signaling include regulators of macropinocytosis such as Ras, Rac1, and Pak1.
source: The many GSK3 phosphorylation targets stabilized by Wnt signaling include regulators of macropinocytosis such as Ras, Rac1, and Pak1 (Taelman et al., 2010; Albrecht et al., 2020; Jeong et al., 2012).
evidence: Cited from Taelman et al., 2010; Albrecht et al., 2020; and Jeong et al., 2012.

claim: Wnt signaling requires macropinocytosis to traffic activated Wnt receptors and GSK3 to MVBs and lysosomes.
source: A recent advance was the realization that Wnt signaling requires macropinocytosis (i.e., cell drinking) in order to traffic activated Wnt receptors and GSK3 to MVBs and lysosomes (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018 and Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019.

claim: Wnt-induced macropinocytosis causes internalization of focal adhesions and integrins into MVBs.
source: Wnt-induced macropinocytosis also causes the internalization of focal adhesions (FAs) and integrins from the cell surface into MVBs (Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2022c).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2022c.

claim: EIPA (5-(N-Ethyl-N-isopropyl) Amiloride) decreases nuclear β-catenin in APC-mutant colorectal cancer cells.
source: The requirement of macropinocytosis for Wnt signaling is revealed, for example, by the decrease in nuclear β-catenin when colorectal cancer (CRC) cells mutant for APC were treated with macropinocytosis inhibitors such as the derivative of the diuretic Amiloride known as 5-(N-Ethyl-N-isopropyl) Amiloride (EIPA) (Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019; Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a; Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022b).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019; Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a; and Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022b.

claim: Macropinocytosis is emerging as a promising target for cancer treatment.
source: Macropinocytosis is emerging in the field as a promising target for cancer treatment (Lambies and Commisso, 2022).
evidence: Cited from Lambies and Commisso, 2022.

claim: Wnt signaling causes significant lysosome acidification and activation.
source: In addition, it has been found that the macropinocytosis induced by Wnt signaling causes significant lysosome acidification and activation (Albrecht et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Albrecht et al., 2020.

claim: The size and number of lysosomes increase during carcinogenesis.
source: There is also accumulating evidence showing that the size and number of lysosomes increase during carcinogenesis (Cardone et al., 2005; Kroemer and Jäättelä, 2005; Zhitomirsky and Assaraf, 2016).
evidence: Cited from Cardone et al., 2005; Kroemer and Jäättelä, 2005; and Zhitomirsky and Assaraf, 2016.

claim: Lysosomes have emerged as central organelles in cancer.
source: Lysosomes, previously thought to be the garbage disposal of the cell, have emerged as central organelles in cancer (Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009; Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009).
evidence: Cited from Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009.

claim: Macropinocytosis in most cells requires stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK).
source: While in most cells macropinocytosis requires stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (Haigler et al., 1979; Yoshida et al., 2018), Ras (Bar-Sagi and Feramisco, 1986; Commisso et al., 2013), or Wnt (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019), some cells, such as amoebae and macrophages, have constitutive macropinocytosis.
evidence: Cited from Haigler et al., 1979 and Yoshida et al., 2018.

claim: Macropinocytosis in most cells requires stimulation of Ras.
source: While in most cells macropinocytosis requires stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (Haigler et al., 1979; Yoshida et al., 2018), Ras (Bar-Sagi and Feramisco, 1986; Commisso et al., 2013), or Wnt (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019), some cells, such as amoebae and macrophages, have constitutive macropinocytosis.
evidence: Cited from Bar-Sagi and Feramisco, 1986 and Commisso et al., 2013.

claim: Macropinocytosis in most cells requires stimulation of Wnt.
source: While in most cells macropinocytosis requires stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (Haigler et al., 1979; Yoshida et al., 2018), Ras (Bar-Sagi and Feramisco, 1986; Commisso et al., 2013), or Wnt (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019), some cells, such as amoebae and macrophages, have constitutive macropinocytosis.
evidence: Cited from Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018 and Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019.

claim: Amoebae and macrophages have constitutive macropinocytosis.
source: While in most cells macropinocytosis requires stimulation of receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (Haigler et al., 1979; Yoshida et al., 2018), Ras (Bar-Sagi and Feramisco, 1986; Commisso et al., 2013), or Wnt (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019), some cells, such as amoebae and macrophages, have constitutive macropinocytosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about these cell types.

claim: PMA stimulates macropinocytosis in macrophages.
source: Importantly, Swanson discovered that the phorbol ester PMA stimulated macropinocytosis even in macrophages that were thought to have fully activated constitutive macropinocytosis (Swanson, 1989).
evidence: Cited from Swanson, 1989.

claim: PMA alone lacks dorsalizing effects on Xenopus embryos.
source: Using the Xenopus embryo, which provides a premier model system to analyze the Wnt pathway, we found that PMA, which lacked any effects on its own, greatly sensitized the embryo to dorsalization by Wnt signaling, leading to the formation of radial head structures lacking trunks.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: PMA greatly sensitizes Xenopus embryos to dorsalization by Wnt signaling.
source: Using the Xenopus embryo, which provides a premier model system to analyze the Wnt pathway, we found that PMA, which lacked any effects on its own, greatly sensitized the embryo to dorsalization by Wnt signaling, leading to the formation of radial head structures lacking trunks.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: PMA and LiCl together lead to radially dorsalized embryos consisting of head structures lacking trunks.
source: Using the Xenopus embryo, which provides a premier model system to analyze the Wnt pathway, we found that PMA, which lacked any effects on its own, greatly sensitized the embryo to dorsalization by Wnt signaling, leading to the formation of radial head structures lacking trunks.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos is blocked by EIPA.
source: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos was blocked by the macropinocytosis inhibitor EIPA, the lysosomal V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A (Baf), or the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos is blocked by Bafilomycin A.
source: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos was blocked by the macropinocytosis inhibitor EIPA, the lysosomal V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A (Baf), or the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos is blocked by the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864.
source: The dorsalizing effect of PMA on embryos was blocked by the macropinocytosis inhibitor EIPA, the lysosomal V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A (Baf), or the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Rac1 is an upstream regulator of p21-activated kinase 1 (Pak1) required for actin-mediated macropinocytosis.
source: Rac1 is an upstream regulator of the p21-activated kinase 1 (Pak1) required for actin-mediated macropinocytosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the macropinocytosis pathway.

claim: Lysosomal activity is specifically required at the 32-cell stage for the activity of LiCl.
source: Lysosomal activity was specifically required at the 32-cell stage for the activity of the Wnt-mimicking GSK3 inhibitor Lithium Chloride (LiCl).
evidence: Demonstrated through order-of-addition experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ectopic axes induced by dominant-negative GSK3 mRNA are blocked by EIPA.
source: Ectopic axes induced by dominant- negative GSK3 (DN-GSK3-β) or β-catenin mRNAs were blocked by EIPA or dominant-negative Rab7, indicating a widespread requirement of membrane trafficking for Wnt signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo microinjection experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ectopic axes induced by dominant-negative GSK3 mRNA are blocked by dominant-negative Rab7.
source: Ectopic axes induced by dominant- negative GSK3 (DN-GSK3-β) or β-catenin mRNAs were blocked by EIPA or dominant-negative Rab7, indicating a widespread requirement of membrane trafficking for Wnt signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo microinjection experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ectopic axes induced by β-catenin mRNA are blocked by EIPA.
source: Ectopic axes induced by dominant- negative GSK3 (DN-GSK3-β) or β-catenin mRNAs were blocked by EIPA or dominant-negative Rab7, indicating a widespread requirement of membrane trafficking for Wnt signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo microinjection experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ectopic axes induced by β-catenin mRNA are blocked by dominant-negative Rab7.
source: Ectopic axes induced by dominant- negative GSK3 (DN-GSK3-β) or β-catenin mRNAs were blocked by EIPA or dominant-negative Rab7, indicating a widespread requirement of membrane trafficking for Wnt signaling.
evidence: Demonstrated in embryo microinjection experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The grade of malignancy in human CRC increases Pak1 levels.
source: In Xenopus embryos, twinning induced by Xwnt8 mRNA microinjection was blocked by inhibition of Rac1. In cultured CRC SW480 cells reconstituted with APC, the FA marker Tes was cytoplasmic, while the same cells mutant for APC (in which the Wnt pathway is activated) Tes was nuclear.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5.

claim: The grade of malignancy in human CRC increases CD63 levels.
source: The involvement of membrane trafficking in Wnt-driven cancer was supported by immunostaining results of arrayed human CRC histological sections, in which we found that the grade of malignancy increased Pak1, CD63 (an MVB marker), and V0a3 (a V-ATPase subunit that marks lysosomes) levels, while decreasing GSK3.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5.

claim: The grade of malignancy in human CRC increases V0a3 levels.
source: The involvement of membrane trafficking in Wnt-driven cancer was supported by immunostaining results of arrayed human CRC histological sections, in which we found that the grade of malignancy increased Pak1, CD63 (an MVB marker), and V0a3 (a V-ATPase subunit that marks lysosomes) levels, while decreasing GSK3.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5.

claim: The grade of malignancy in human CRC decreases GSK3 levels.
source: The involvement of membrane trafficking in Wnt-driven cancer was supported by immunostaining results of arrayed human CRC histological sections, in which we found that the grade of malignancy increased Pak1, CD63 (an MVB marker), and V0a3 (a V-ATPase subunit that marks lysosomes) levels, while decreasing GSK3.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5.

claim: In SW480 cells reconstituted with APC, the FA marker Tes is cytoplasmic.
source: In cultured CRC SW480 cells reconstituted with APC, the FA marker Tes was cytoplasmic, while the same cells mutant for APC (in which the Wnt pathway is activated) Tes was nuclear.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining shown in Figure 6.

claim: In SW480 cells mutant for APC, the FA marker Tes is nuclear.
source: In cultured CRC SW480 cells reconstituted with APC, the FA marker Tes was cytoplasmic, while the same cells mutant for APC (in which the Wnt pathway is activated) Tes was nuclear.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunostaining shown in Figure 6.

claim: Inhibition of macropinocytosis with EIPA ventralizes endogenous early dorsal axis formation in Xenopus embryos.
source: Recently, we reported that inhibition of macropinocytosis with EIPA, or of lysosomal acidification with Baf, ventralized endogenous early dorsal axis formation, leading in particular to reduced head and brain structures (Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: Inhibition of lysosomal acidification with Baf ventralizes endogenous early dorsal axis formation in Xenopus embryos.
source: Recently, we reported that inhibition of macropinocytosis with EIPA, or of lysosomal acidification with Baf, ventralized endogenous early dorsal axis formation, leading in particular to reduced head and brain structures (Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: Lysosome activation on the dorsal side of the embryo is detectable as early as the 64-cell stage.
source: Activation of lysosomes on the dorsal side of the embryo was detectable as early as the 64-cell stage (Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: LiCl alone causes only slight dorsalization with slightly enlarged heads in Xenopus embryos.
source: To test its activity during early development, we used a sensitized system in which a small amount of the GSK3 inhibitor LiCl (4 nl at 300 mM in a single ventral injection at 4-cell) causes only a small dorsalization with slightly enlarged heads (Kao et al., 1986; Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Cited from Kao et al., 1986 and Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a, and demonstrated in Figure 1B.

claim: PMA and LiCl synergistically increase Siamois transcript levels at blastula stage.
source: As shown in Figure 1I, PMA alone (4 nl at 500 nM) was without any effect, LiCl increased the Wnt target genes, and the combination of PMA and LiCl synergized significantly elevated Siamois and Xnr3 transcript levels, while EIPA and Baf blocked the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl (Figure 1I).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: PMA and LiCl synergistically increase Xnr3 transcript levels at blastula stage.
source: As shown in Figure 1I, PMA alone (4 nl at 500 nM) was without any effect, LiCl increased the Wnt target genes, and the combination of PMA and LiCl synergized significantly elevated Siamois and Xnr3 transcript levels, while EIPA and Baf blocked the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl (Figure 1I).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: EIPA blocks the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl.
source: As shown in Figure 1I, PMA alone (4 nl at 500 nM) was without any effect, LiCl increased the Wnt target genes, and the combination of PMA and LiCl synergized significantly elevated Siamois and Xnr3 transcript levels, while EIPA and Baf blocked the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl (Figure 1I).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Baf blocks the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl.
source: As shown in Figure 1I, PMA alone (4 nl at 500 nM) was without any effect, LiCl increased the Wnt target genes, and the combination of PMA and LiCl synergized significantly elevated Siamois and Xnr3 transcript levels, while EIPA and Baf blocked the increase in Siamois and Xnr3 caused by PMA/LiCl (Figure 1I).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: PMA cooperates with LiCl in HEK293BR cells as measured by luciferase activity.
source: Using the BAR (β-catenin activity reporter) assay system (Biechele and Moon, 2008) in a cultured HEK293 permanent BAR/Renilla cell line, PMA synergized with LiCl when assayed by transcriptional BAR luciferase activity (Figure 1J).
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assay shown in Figure 1J, with citation to Biechele and Moon, 2008.

claim: Baf inhibits the cooperation between PMA and LiCl in HEK293BR cells.
source: Importantly, the effect of PMA on the activation of the Wnt pathway by GSK3 inhibition was abrogated by the inhibition of V-ATPase with Baf (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PMA cooperates with Wnt3a to stimulate macropinocytosis in 3T3 cells.
source: To test the effect of PMA on Wnt-induced macropinocytosis we used an uptake assay in which 3T3 cells were treated with dextran for 1 hr (Figure 1K–P). The macropinocytosis marker TMR-dextran 70 kDa has a hydrated diameter of more than 200 nM and is diagnostic of large endocytic cups, in particular when sensitive to the macropinocytosis inhibitor EIPA (Commisso et al., 2013; Commisso et al., 2014). In the presence of Wnt3a, but not in the absence, PMA strongly induced dextran uptake and this effect was blocked by EIPA (Figure 1K–P, quantitated in Figure 1Q).
evidence: Demonstrated by TMR-dextran uptake assay shown in Figure 1K-Q, with citations to Commisso et al., 2013 and 2014.

claim: EIPA blocks PMA and Wnt3a-induced macropinocytosis in 3T3 cells.
source: In the presence of Wnt3a, but not in the absence, PMA strongly induced dextran uptake and this effect was blocked by EIPA (Figure 1K–P, quantitated in Figure 1Q).
evidence: Demonstrated by TMR-dextran uptake assay shown in Figure 1K-Q.

claim: PMA increases dextran uptake in SW480 CRC cells.
source: PMA also increased dextran uptake in the SW480 CRC cell line that has constitutive Wnt signaling, even in the absence of added Wnt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K).
evidence: Demonstrated by TMR-dextran uptake assay shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J, K.

claim: PMA triggers abundant formation of macropinosome cups within minutes in SW480 cells.
source: In time-lapse video microscopy of SW480 cells with the plasma membrane tagged by myristoylated-GFP (mGFP), PMA addition triggered the abundant formation of macropinosome cups within minutes of addition when compared to DMSO (Dimethylsulfoxide) controls (Video 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by time-lapse video microscopy shown in Video 1.

claim: Immersion of embryos in Baf at 5 µM for 7 min at the 32-cell stage results in ventralized microcephalic embryos lacking cement glands.
source: In previous work, we had shown that immersion of embryos in the V-ATPase inhibitor Baf at 5 µM for only 7 min at the 32-cell stage resulted in ventralized microcephalic embryos lacking cement glands (Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: When Baf treatment is followed by LiCl treatment at 32-cell stage, the ventralization by Baf is rescued.
source: When an initial Baf incubation of 7 min was followed by a second brief incubation in LiCl while still at the 32-cell stage, the ventralization by Baf was rescued, and the resulting tailbud embryos had a LiCl-like dorsalized phenotype (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: Demonstrated by order-of-addition experiments shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: When LiCl treatment is followed by Baf treatment at 32-cell stage, the effect of lysosomal inhibition is dominant, resulting in ventralized embryos.
source: In the converse experiment, when embryos were first briefly treated with LiCl, washed, and subsequently incubated for 7 min in Baf, the effect of lysosomal inhibition was dominant, resulting in ventralized tailbud embryos (Figure 2F–J).
evidence: Demonstrated by order-of-addition experiments shown in Figure 2F-J.

claim: Membrane trafficking and endogenous lysosomal activity are required to generate the initial endogenous Wnt signal at the 32-cell stage.
source: These order-of-addition experiments strongly support the proposal that membrane trafficking and endogenous lysosomal activity are required to generate the initial endogenous Wnt signal that takes place at the 32-cell stage of development (Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a).
evidence: Inferred from order-of-addition experiments shown in Figure 2, with citation to Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: EHT1864 is a specific inhibitor of Rac1 that is water soluble.
source: EHT1864 (EHT) is a specific inhibitor of Rac1 that has the practical advantage of being water soluble (Hampsch et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from Hampsch et al., 2017.

claim: EHT treatment at 32-cell stage greatly reduces head structures and expands ventral posterior structures in Xenopus embryos.
source: When embryos were immersed in EHT at the critical 32-cell stage for 7 min (10 mM), head structures were greatly reduced, and ventral posterior structures expanded (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: Demonstrated by embryo phenotypes shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: EHT treatment increases transcripts of ventral markers Sizzled and Vent1 at blastula stage.
source: This was accompanied by a significant increase of transcripts of the ventral markers Sizzled and Vent1 at the blastula stage (Figure 4C).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR shown in Figure 4C.

claim: EHT blocks double axis formation induced by Wnt8 mRNA.
source: Microinjection of a small amount of EHT (1 mM, 4 nl, 1x ventral at 4-cell) was without effect on its own but was able to block the axis duplication effect of microinjecting Wnt8 mRNA (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: Demonstrated by embryo microinjection experiments shown in Figure 4D-G.

claim: Inhibiting Rac1 strongly reduces induction of Wnt target genes Siamois and Xnr3 caused by xWnt8 mRNA.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR analyses at the blastula stage confirmed that inhibiting Rac1 strongly reduced the induction of the Wnt target genes Siamois and Xnr3 caused by xWnt8 mRNA microinjection at the late blastula stage (Figure 4H).
evidence: Demonstrated by qRT-PCR shown in Figure 4H.

claim: EHT inhibits the size of SW480 cell spheroids in hanging drop cultures.
source: In SW480 CRC cells, which have constitutively activated Wnt due to mutation of APC (Leibovitz et al., 1976; Faux et al., 2004), EHT inhibited the size of cell spheroids in hanging drop cultures (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C) and, importantly, significantly inhibited macropinocytosis uptake of TMR-dextran in these cancer cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: Demonstrated by spheroid culture experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C, with citations to Leibovitz et al., 1976 and Faux et al., 2004.

claim: EHT significantly inhibits macropinocytosis uptake of TMR-dextran in SW480 cells.
source: In SW480 CRC cells, which have constitutively activated Wnt due to mutation of APC (Leibovitz et al., 1976; Faux et al., 2004), EHT inhibited the size of cell spheroids in hanging drop cultures (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C) and, importantly, significantly inhibited macropinocytosis uptake of TMR-dextran in these cancer cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: Demonstrated by TMR-dextran uptake assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: LiCl treatment increases Rac1 protein levels in 3T3 cells.
source: Rac1 itself was stabilized in 3T3 cells by Wnt signaling, as indicated by experiments showing (1) that LiCl treatment increased levels of Rac1 protein (Figure 4I–J''), (2) that cells transfected with constitutively active β-catenin-GFP had higher levels of Rac1 than control untransfected cells (Figure 4K–K''), and (3) that Rac1 immunostaining was stabilized in cells transfected with CA-Lrp6-GFP when compared to untransfected cells (Figure 4L–L'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 4I-J''.

claim: Cells transfected with constitutively active β-catenin-GFP have higher levels of Rac1 than control untransfected cells.
source: Rac1 itself was stabilized in 3T3 cells by Wnt signaling, as indicated by experiments showing (1) that LiCl treatment increased levels of Rac1 protein (Figure 4I–J''), (2) that cells transfected with constitutively active β-catenin-GFP had higher levels of Rac1 than control untransfected cells (Figure 4K–K''), and (3) that Rac1 immunostaining was stabilized in cells transfected with CA-Lrp6-GFP when compared to untransfected cells (Figure 4L–L'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 4K-K''.

claim: Rac1 immunostaining is stabilized in cells transfected with CA-Lrp6-GFP compared to untransfected cells.
source: Rac1 itself was stabilized in 3T3 cells by Wnt signaling, as indicated by experiments showing (1) that LiCl treatment increased levels of Rac1 protein (Figure 4I–J''), (2) that cells transfected with constitutively active β-catenin-GFP had higher levels of Rac1 than control untransfected cells (Figure 4K–K''), and (3) that Rac1 immunostaining was stabilized in cells transfected with CA-Lrp6-GFP when compared to untransfected cells (Figure 4L–L'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 4L-L''.

claim: CRC is favorable for analysis of tumor progression because it gradually accumulates mutations.
source: CRC is particularly favorable for the analysis of tumor progression because it gradually accumulates mutations, and in over 85% of the cases the initial driver mutation is in the APC tumor suppressor (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996; Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007).
evidence: Cited from Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996 and Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007.

claim: In over 85% of CRC cases, the initial driver mutation is in the APC tumor suppressor.
source: CRC is particularly favorable for the analysis of tumor progression because it gradually accumulates mutations, and in over 85% of the cases the initial driver mutation is in the APC tumor suppressor (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996; Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007).
evidence: Cited from Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1996 and Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007.

claim: β-catenin levels consistently correlate with grade IV malignancy in human CRC.
source: As shown in Figure 5, β-catenin levels consistently correlated with grade IV malignancy when compared to normal colon or grade I cancers.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Pak1 is significantly elevated with increased CRC malignancy.
source: Pak1, a kinase required for macropinocytosis and Wnt signaling (Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018; Albrecht et al., 2020) was significantly elevated with increased malignancy (Figure 5A–C'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5A-C'', with citations to Redelman-Sidi et al., 2018 and Albrecht et al., 2020.

claim: CD63 reaches high levels in adenocarcinoma IV, particularly in cells with highest β-catenin expression.
source: CD63, a tetraspan protein that marks MVB intraluminal vesicles (Escola et al., 1998), reached high levels in adenocarcinoma IV (Figure 5D–F''), particularly in cells with the highest β-catenin expression (compare Figure 5F–F').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5D-F'', with citation to Escola et al., 1998.

claim: The increase in MVBs in CRC is in agreement with the GSK3 sequestration model of Wnt signaling.
source: This increase in MVBs is in agreement with the GSK3 sequestration model of Wnt signaling (Taelman et al., 2010).
evidence: Inference based on data, with citation to Taelman et al., 2010.

claim: V0a3 increases strongly with CRC malignancy.
source: The V-ATPase subunit V0a3, a marker for acidic lysosomes (Ramirez et al., 2019), also increased strongly with the CRC malignancy (compare Figure 5G–I).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5G-I, with citation to Ramirez et al., 2019.

claim: Total cellular GSK3 levels decrease with CRC malignancy.
source: Importantly, the cellular levels of total GSK3 decreased with malignancy (Figure 5J–L'', compare Figure 5J–L), as predicted by the sequestration model (Taelman et al., 2010).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of tissue arrays shown in Figure 5J-L'', with citation to Taelman et al., 2010.

claim: During Wnt signaling, GSK3 is sequestered into MVBs which are trafficked into lysosomes.
source: During Wnt signaling, GSK3 is sequestered into MVBs which are trafficked into lysosomes and a decrease was to be expected after sustained Wnt activation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the sequestration model and observed data.

claim: In nude mouse xenografts, CRC cells have high levels of β-catenin, Pak1, and lysosomes.
source: The results showed that CRC cells had high levels of β-catenin, Pak1, and lysosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–J), while GSK3 levels were reduced (compare Figure 5—figure supplement 1K–L) in agreement with the results in human tissue arrays.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of mouse xenografts shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-J.

claim: In nude mouse xenografts, GSK3 levels are reduced in CRC cells.
source: The results showed that CRC cells had high levels of β-catenin, Pak1, and lysosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–J), while GSK3 levels were reduced (compare Figure 5—figure supplement 1K–L) in agreement with the results in human tissue arrays.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining of mouse xenografts shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1K-L.

claim: Wnt3a treatment rapidly leads to endocytosis of Integrin β1 and multiple FA proteins into MVBs.
source: We have previously reported a crosstalk between the Wnt and FA signaling pathways in which Wnt3a treatment rapidly led to the endocytosis of Integrin β1 and of multiple FA proteins into MVBs (Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2022c).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2022c.

claim: FA components containing LIM domains can shuttle between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
source: FA components containing LIM domains can shuttle between the nucleus and cytoplasm (Nix and Beckerle, 1997; Kadrmas and Beckerle, 2004; Anderson et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from Nix and Beckerle, 1997; Kadrmas and Beckerle, 2004; and Anderson et al., 2021.

claim: Stable reconstitution of SW480 cells with full-length APC restores them to a non-malignant phenotype.
source: We examined whether constitutive Wnt signaling regulates FA trafficking using the SW480 and SW480APC system, in which the stable reconstitution with full-length APC restores these CRC cells to a non-malignant phenotype (Faux et al., 2004), which is accompanied by a decrease in β-catenin levels (Figure 6B).
evidence: Cited from Faux et al., 2004, and demonstrated by Western blot in Figure 6B.

claim: The nuclear localization of Tes in SW480 cells requires macropinocytosis.
source: The nuclear localization of Tes in SW480 cells required macropinocytosis, as suggested by treatment with EIPA which resulted in its re-localization to the cytoplasm (Figure 6E–F'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6E-F''.

claim: In nude mouse xenografts, Tes is abundant in the cytoplasm of normal colon epithelium.
source: In the nude mouse xenograft model, Tes was abundant in the cytoplasm of normal colon epielium, while in transplanted SW480 cells it colocalized with β-catenin in the nucleus of those cells with the highest β-catenin levels (Figure 6G–I'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6G-I''.

claim: In transplanted SW480 cells in nude mouse xenografts, Tes colocalizes with β-catenin in the nucleus of cells with highest β-catenin levels.
source: In the nude mouse xenograft model, Tes was abundant in the cytoplasm of normal colon epielium, while in transplanted SW480 cells it colocalized with β-catenin in the nucleus of those cells with the highest β-catenin levels (Figure 6G–I'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6G-I''.

claim: TES has been proposed to act as a tumor suppressor.
source: The function of TES is poorly understood, but it has been proposed to act as a tumor suppressor (Tatarelli et al., 2000; Tobias et al., 2001).
evidence: Cited from Tatarelli et al., 2000 and Tobias et al., 2001.

claim: FAK inhibitor PF-00562271 strongly decreases β-catenin signaling by LiCl in HEK293 BAR/Renilla cells.
source: In HEK293 BAR/Renilla cells, treatment with the FAK inhibitor PF-00562271 strongly decreased β-catenin signaling by LiCl inhibition of GSK3 (Figure 6J; see also Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B'').
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase assay shown in Figure 6J.

claim: FAK inhibitor treatment results in ventralized Xenopus embryos with reduced dorsal-anterior structures.
source: In the context on the Xenopus embryo, treatment with the FAK inhibitor (100 µM, 7 min at 32-cell stage) resulted in ventralized embryos with reduced dorsal-anterior structures such as central nervous system, in particular brain structures stained by the pan-neural marker Sox2 (Figure 6K'–L'').
evidence: Demonstrated by embryo phenotypes and in situ hybridization shown in Figure 6K'-L''.

claim: PMA addition to SW480 cells strongly increases protein levels of β-catenin and FAK.
source: The addition of the tumor promoter PMA to SW480 cells (in which the Wnt pathway is constitutively activated) strongly increased protein levels of β-catenin and FAK protein (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–D'').
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-D''.

claim: The effect of PMA on β-catenin and FAK levels is abrogated by EIPA or Baf treatment.
source: The effect of PMA on β-catenin and FAK levels was abrogated by EIPA or Baf treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–H''), suggesting that it requires macropinocytosis and lysosome activity.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-H''.

claim: Nuclear Tes could serve as a Wnt-regulated marker in CRC.
source: The results also suggest that nuclear Tes could serve as a Wnt-regulated marker in CRC.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed data.

claim: The regulated shuttling of FA components between nucleus and cytoplasm is probably just the tip of the iceberg of the role of membrane trafficking in Wnt-driven cancers.
source: The regulated shuttling of FA components between nucleus and cytoplasm is probably just the tip of the iceberg of the role of membrane trafficking in Wnt-driven cancers.
evidence: This is a speculation about broader implications.

claim: PMA activates the PKC pathway.
source: PMA activates the PKC pathway (Takai et al., 1979; Nishizuka, 1984), and there is previous literature on the crosstalk between the PKC and Wnt pathways (Schwarz et al., 2013; Goode et al., 1992).
evidence: Cited from Takai et al., 1979 and Nishizuka, 1984.

claim: There is previous literature on crosstalk between PKC and Wnt pathways.
source: PMA activates the PKC pathway (Takai et al., 1979; Nishizuka, 1984), and there is previous literature on the crosstalk between the PKC and Wnt pathways (Schwarz et al., 2013; Goode et al., 1992).
evidence: Cited from Schwarz et al., 2013 and Goode et al., 1992.

claim: The crosstalk between macropinocytosis, membrane trafficking, lysosomes, FAs, PMA, and Wnt signaling is novel.
source: What is novel in the present paper is the crosstalk between macropinocytosis, membrane trafficking, lysosomes, FAs, PMA, and Wnt signaling.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the current work.

claim: Different PKC isoforms can have positive or negative effects on Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
source: There is previous literature implicating PKC isozymes in the regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway (Fang et al., 2002; Goode et al., 1992) and that different PKC isoforms can have positive or negative effects on Wnt/β-catenin signaling (Ohno and Nishizuka, 2002).
evidence: Cited from Fang et al., 2002; Goode et al., 1992; and Ohno and Nishizuka, 2002.

claim: The molecular role of PKC isoforms in the Wnt signaling pathway remains poorly understood.
source: However, the molecular role of PKC isoforms in the Wnt signaling pathway remains poorly understood (Bhatia and Spiegelman, 2005; Schwarz et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from Bhatia and Spiegelman, 2005 and Schwarz et al., 2013.

claim: PMA can stabilize CK1ε and enhance its kinase activity.
source: It has been reported that PMA can stabilize CK1ε (Casein Kinase 1 epsilon), enhance its kinase activity, and induce LRP6 phosphorylation at Thr1479 and Ser1490, leading to the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway (Su et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Su et al., 2018.

claim: PMA induces LRP6 phosphorylation at Thr1479 and Ser1490, leading to activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.
source: It has been reported that PMA can stabilize CK1ε (Casein Kinase 1 epsilon), enhance its kinase activity, and induce LRP6 phosphorylation at Thr1479 and Ser1490, leading to the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway (Su et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Su et al., 2018.

claim: Wnt signaling rapidly triggers macropinocytosis and trafficking into lysosomes.
source: In the context of the present study, it is relevant that Wnt signaling rapidly triggers macropinocytosis and trafficking into lysosomes (Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Tejeda-Muñoz et al., 2019.

claim: Macropinocytosis requires activation of PI3K which leads to formation of PIP3 patches in the inner plasma membrane leaflet.
source: Macropinocytosis requires the activation of phosphoinositide 3 kinase (PI3K) which leads to the formation of patches of PIP3 in the inner plasma membrane leaflet that initiate the formation of macropinocytic cups (Egami et al., 2014; Yoshida et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Egami et al., 2014 and Yoshida et al., 2018.

claim: During macropinosome formation, PIP3 is converted into DAG by phospholipase C gamma 1 (PLCγ1).
source: During macropinosome formation, the PIP3 lipid is then converted into DAG by phospholipase C gamma 1 (PLCγ1), and DAG activates PKC signaling (Yoshida et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Yoshida et al., 2018.

claim: DAG activates PKC signaling during macropinosome formation.
source: During macropinosome formation, the PIP3 lipid is then converted into DAG by phospholipase C gamma 1 (PLCγ1), and DAG activates PKC signaling (Yoshida et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Yoshida et al., 2018.

claim: PMA may facilitate Wnt/β-catenin signaling by mimicking the DAG lipid in macropinosomes.
source: It seems likely that PMA may facilitate Wnt/β-catenin signaling by mimicking the DAG lipid in macropinosomes.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the known mechanism of PMA and macropinocytosis.

claim: Direct addition of DAG to cells shows cooperation with Wnt signaling.
source: We have tested this hypothesis by direct addition of DAG to cells and found cooperation with Wnt signaling (Azbazdar et al., 2023).
evidence: Cited from Azbazdar et al., 2023.

claim: Active PKC phosphorylates IκB kinase (IKK), which becomes activated and phosphorylates IκB, targeting it for degradation and triggering inflammation.
source: Active PKC phosphorylates many targets, including IκB kinase (IKK), which becomes activated and phosphorylates inhibitor of NF-κB (IκB), targeting it for degradation and triggering inflammation (Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007).
evidence: Cited from Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007.

claim: Tumor progression is promoted by many chronic inflammatory agents that do not cause mutations but regulate expansion of previously mutant clones.
source: Tumor progression is promoted by many chronic inflammatory agents such as turpentine, distilled alcoholic beverages, hepatitis viruses, and Helicobacter pylori that do not cause mutations by themselves but regulate the expansion of previously mutant clones (Rous and Kidd, 1941; Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007).
evidence: Cited from Rous and Kidd, 1941 and Weinberg and Weinberg, 2007.

claim: Macropinocytosis, lysosomal activity, and membrane trafficking are possible therapeutic targets for tumor progression in Wnt-driven cancers.
source: Taken together, the results presented here suggest that macropinocytosis, lysosomal activity, and membrane trafficking are possible therapeutic targets for tumor progression in Wnt-driven cancers.
evidence: This is a speculation about therapeutic implications based on the study's findings.

claim: Rac1 is a member of the family of small Rho GTPases that drives formation of lamellipodia, membrane ruffles, and macropinocytosis.
source: Rac1 is a member of the family of small Rho GTPases that drives the formation of lamellipodia, membrane ruffles, and macropinocytosis (Hall, 1998; Egami et al., 2014; Fujii et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from Hall, 1998; Egami et al., 2014; and Fujii et al., 2013.

claim: Rac1 binds to β-catenin and promotes formation of nuclear β-catenin/LEF1 complexes.
source: Other work has shown that Rac1 binds to β-catenin and promotes the formation of nuclear β-catenin/LEF1 complexes (Jamieson et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from Jamieson et al., 2015.

claim: Rac1 increases nuclear translocation of β-catenin.
source: Rac1 is a regulator of multiple signaling cascades and has been reported to increase the nuclear translocation of β-catenin (Wu et al., 2008).
evidence: Cited from Wu et al., 2008.

claim: The lysosome is considered a promising target for the treatment of cancer.
source: The lysosome is considered a promising target for the treatment of cancer (Fehrenbacher and Jäättelä, 2005; Lawrence and Zoncu, 2019).
evidence: Cited from Fehrenbacher and Jäättelä, 2005 and Lawrence and Zoncu, 2019.

claim: Cancer cells require lysosome function and have changes in lysosomal volume and subcellular localization during oncogenic transformation.
source: Cancer cells require lysosome function and have changes in lysosomal volume and subcellular localization during oncogenic transformation (Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009; Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009; Gocheva and Joyce, 2007; Kolwijck et al., 2010).
evidence: Cited from Kirkegaard and Jäättelä, 2009; Gocheva and Joyce, 2007; and Kolwijck et al., 2010.

claim: V-ATPase has been associated with acidification of the extracellular milieu in tumors.
source: V-ATPase has been associated with acidification of the extracellular milieu in tumors (Capecci and Forgac, 2013; Hinton et al., 2009; Perona and Serrano, 1988).
evidence: Cited from Capecci and Forgac, 2013; Hinton et al., 2009; and Perona and Serrano, 1988.

claim: Extracellular tumor acidification is probably due to increased numbers of lysosomes which are exocytosed.
source: Extracellular tumor acidification is probably due to increased numbers of lysosomes which are exocytosed, since V0a3 was located within the cytoplasm in advanced cancer or xenografts in mice (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed localization of V0a3.

claim: Wnt-driven lysosomal acidification and GSK3 sequestration may play a role in cancer.
source: The results reported here support the view (Taelman et al., 2010; Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a) that Wnt-driven lysosomal acidification and GSK3 sequestration may play a role in cancer.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings, with citations to Taelman et al., 2010 and Tejeda-Muñoz and De Robertis, 2022a.

claim: MVB/lysosome components could serve as markers for advanced Wnt-driven cancers.
source: In addition, MVB/lysosome components could serve as markers for advanced Wnt-driven cancers.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the correlation observed in tissue arrays.

claim: Focal adhesions link the actin cytoskeleton with the extracellular matrix.
source: The cytoskeleton interacts with proteins of the extracellular matrix though FAs (Geiger et al., 2001).
evidence: Cited from Geiger et al., 2001.

claim: Other FA proteins shuttle between nucleus, cytoplasm, and FA sites, and may play important roles in cancer.
source: Other FA proteins shuttle between the nucleus, cytoplasm, and FA sites, and may play important roles in cancer (Chaturvedi et al., 2012; Nix and Beckerle, 1997).
evidence: Cited from Chaturvedi et al., 2012 and Nix and Beckerle, 1997.

claim: FAK is a key signaling kinase that regulates FA signaling.
source: FAK is a key signaling kinase that regulates FA signaling.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FAK.

claim: There is a possible crosstalk between FAs, Wnt signaling and tumor promoters in cancer progression and embryonic development.
source: These results suggest a possible crosstalk between FAs, Wnt signaling and tumor promoters in cancer progression and embryonic development.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.
